rulers.name: Yakub Beg (Athalik Ghazi)
rulers.title: Emir
rulers.note: YB: 'enthroned himself as the ruler of Yettishar when the Chinese were expelled from the region in 1864'; arrived at Kashgar in 1865; title Athalik Ghazi from the Emir of Bukhara in 1866; died 1877 (poisoned at Korla on 30 May 1877 per Musa Sayrami, a stroke per most scholars).

correction.text: the Kashgar oasis, Yakub Beg's first seat

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: Kashgar and its oasis, where Yakub Beg 'soon managed to take complete control of the oasis towns' after settling there in 1865 (YB); DR: he took the Manchu fortress and the Han town of Kashgar during 1865. A 150 km radius (about 60,000 km2) stands for the oasis.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin that Yakub Beg 'conquered' (YB): Kashgar, Khotan, Yarkand, Yengisar, Aksu, Kucha and Korla, the seven cities

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'he conquered the Tarim Basin' (YB), the seven cities Kashgar, Khotan, Yarkand, Yengisar, Aksu, Kucha and Korla; no page dates the individual towns, so 1866 is a bridge. The Tarim Basin region is about 942,000 km2 in the gazetteer and so over-reaches the oases; YB gives no area. Turfan and Urumqi (held 1870 on other sources) are not on the pages and are left out.

ledger.note: 1864: Yettishar is established at Kashgar. Infobox 'Established: 12 November 1864'; Yakub Beg 'enthroned himself as the ruler of Yettishar when the Chinese were expelled from the region in 1864' (he reached Kashgar in 1865 and, per DR, took its Manchu fortress and Han town during 1865). The region is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 1866: the rest of the Tarim Basin is brought in. YB says he 'conquered the Tarim Basin' and lists Khotan, Yarkand, Yengisar, Aksu, Kucha and Korla as the seven cities but dates none; 1866 (the year the Emir of Bukhara gave him the title Athalik Ghazi) is a bridge.

ledger.note: 1877: the Qing reconquer Kashgar. Yakub Beg dies in May 1877; on 18 December 1877 'the Qing army entered Kashgar and brought the state to an end'.

wars.name: Qing reconquest of Xinjiang

zones.text: the Tarim Basin and the north of Xinjiang

wars.outcome: Zuo Zongtang's army ended Yettishar; Kashgar entered on 18 December 1877; Xinjiang became a province in 1884.
wars.note: 'In the late 1870s, the Qing decided to reconquer Xinjiang with Zuo Zongtang' as commander-in-chief. Under the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg Russia returned the Ili region to China.

wars.name: Dungan Revolt (1862-1877)
wars.outcome: The risings of 1864 (Kucha, Urumqi, Yarkand, Ili) broke Qing rule in Xinjiang; Yakub Beg built Yettishar on them and the Qing reconquered it by December 1877.

certainty.note: An oasis state without surveyed frontiers; Tarim, Taklamakan and Tian Shan edges are approximate. YB notes Ottoman recognition as a vassal in 1873, which the Ottoman dossier should carry.

sources.title: Yettishar
sources.note: Established 12 November 1864; Yakub Beg in Kashgar from 1865; seven cities; Ottoman vassalage 1873; reconquered by Zuo Zongtang, Kashgar entered 18 December 1877.

sources.title: Dungan Revolt (1862-1877)
sources.note: The risings of 1864 (Kucha 3-4 June, Urumqi 26 June, Yarkand 26 July, Ili 10 November); Kashgar taken by Yaqub Beg in 1865.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (YB, DR; budget 2-5). Not on the pages: the dates of Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu, Kucha, Turfan and Urumqi under Yakub Beg, Russian recognition (1872) and British (1874), the treaties with Russia and Britain (YB says he signed 'respective treaties' without dates). The Ottoman vassalage ('In 1873, the Ottoman Empire recognised Yettishar as a vassal state'; the Ottoman flag flew over Kashgar 1873-1877) is a relation for the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) to carry as a vassal pair with counterpart yettishar. Counterparts: qing-dynasty (ea-08; no dossier existed on 2026-10-19), ili-sultanate (written in this batch). YB's lead says 1864-1877.
